summary: This is a long Wikipedia-style article excerpt about Paris, France. It covers immigration figures from the 2012 census, the city's water supply and manufacturing decline, airports and broadcasting, and the city's population and Eurostat and INSEE rankings. It also covers Paris's literary and theatre history, its courts, its Christian origins, climate, incomes and unemployment, the 1961 Algerian protest, and its music history.
one_line: Wikipedia excerpt covering Paris's demographics, water supply, economy, airports, media, literary and theatre life, history, climate and music.
key_facts: According to the 2012 census, 135,853 residents of the city of Paris were immigrants from Europe and 112,369 were immigrants from the Maghreb.
From 1857, civil engineer Eugène Belgrand, under Napoleon III, oversaw construction of new aqueducts that brought water to several reservoirs built atop Paris's highest points.
Paris proper manufacturing jobs dropped by 64 percent between 1990 and 2010, and the Paris region lost 48 percent during the same period.
Charles de Gaulle Airport opened to commercial traffic in 1974 and became the busiest Parisian airport in 1993; it is the 4th busiest airport in the world by international traffic.
Paris had an administrative city limits population of 2,241,346 in January 2014, making it the fifth largest municipality in the European Union.
The Paris Urban Area had a population of 10,550,350 at the January 2012 census, the most populous in the European Union.
The Comédie-Française, the oldest and most famous Paris theatre, was founded in 1680.
Louis XIV moved his court to Versailles in 1682.
Patrick Modiano, who lives in Paris, won the 2014 Nobel Prize in Literature.
According to tradition, Saint Denis, the first Bishop of Paris, was beheaded on the hill later known as Montmartre, from the Latin 'Mons Martyrum'.
On 17 October 1961, an unauthorised but peaceful protest by Algerians against a curfew led to violent confrontations with police, in which at least 40 people were killed.
The Paris Region had a GDP of €649.6 billion in 2014, accounting for 30.4 percent of the GDP of France.
Unemployment was estimated at 8.2 percent in the city of Paris and 8.8 percent in the Île-de-France region in the first trimester of 2015.
The average net household income in Paris was €36,085 for 2011, ranging from €22,095 in the 19th arrondissement to €82,449 in the 7th arrondissement.
